samguk.head: A full-body character image, vertical 2:3 (1024×1536): Wen Yang of the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, reimagined as an adult woman — the young warrior who turned alone and drove back hundreds.
samguk.faceFrame: Her face is small and soft: a short midface, a softly rounded jaw and a small chin, about 1.3 times as long as it is wide, with her eyes open at their natural size. Bangs, side locks and headpieces frame the face without lengthening it.
character: Age: late twenties — a graceful grown-up face with soft, smooth contours.

Face — her own, recognisably this character, a woman's face with no beard or facial hair: a fierce, wild ferocity; fair skin; heart-shaped face; large eyes — large round eyes, outer eye corners drooping downward; thin arched brows; small button nose; full wide lips; ice-blue eyes; sharp winged eyeliner.
Body and hair: tall and statuesque with long legs and a full, curvaceous figure — full bust and hips, narrow waist build; a bob with long bangs falling over one eye; glossy jet-black hair.
Expression: a composed, self-assured look, subtle and relaxed.
Legend, carried in her design and bearing: peerless solo courage, a steel whip-sword.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.
costume: Costume: Three Kingdoms war general's armor — lamellar scale armor laced over a silk battle robe, beast-head shoulder guards, a plumed helmet or a war headband, a long war cape, her weapon at hand. Late-Han Chinese dress — cross-collared silk robes with wide sleeves and a broad sash, lamellar or scale armor laced with cords where armor is worn, bronze, jade and lacquer ornament, Han court hair ornaments; silk, lacquered leather, bronze and iron.
Silhouette: layered laced lamellar armor, big heavy beast-head pauldrons and armored skirts to the knees — a broad, weighty general's silhouette. The overall shape is fixed; the details are free.
Colours: deep navy blue, black lacquer, cold steel silver, ivory white.

Signature item: a steel whip-sword. She holds it at full scale: one whole object, drawn once, held in front of or beside her body; a long weapon keeps one straight, unbroken shaft with a single head or blade.
scene: World: Cao Wei in northern China, around 200–235 AD: the walled capitals of Xuchang, Ye and Luoyang, rammed-earth ramparts and tiled watchtowers, black-and-navy banners over vast northern plains, armoured cavalry, bronze ritual vessels and lacquered halls.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.

Composition: her whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet inside the frame with clear margins, about four-fifths of the image height; camera at chest height with natural portrait perspective.
constraints: One figure only — no second character, horse or other creature. No readable text or numbers, except that a banner, seal or emblem may carry the single character 魏 or 文. No logo, watermark, speech bubble or frame border. Three Kingdoms-era Chinese dress, architecture and materials only.
